Immune complexes lodge in small skin vessels, recruit neutrophils and break down (leukocytoclasis).

points: Drug-induced LCV usually starts **7–21 days** after a new drug (sooner on re-exposure; this case says "a few days").

**3e — the single bedside test: urinalysis** (dipstick for **blood and protein**). It tells you whether the kidneys are involved (systemic vasculitis/IgA nephritis), which changes urgency and management. Measure BP at the same visit.

items.t: Haematuria, proteinuria or rising creatinine: same-day renal advice.
Necrosis, ulceration or purpura above the waist: consider systemic vasculitis and refer urgently.

pearls.t: "**Drug, legs, palpable purpura, well patient → stop the drug, dip the urine, elevate.**"
Warn that **new crops can appear for 1–2 weeks** after stopping the drug.
